Coffee & pies

What comes to the table

From what guests write in their Google reviews.

Homemade pies

Spinach pie, cheese pie, halloumi pie and olive rolls, baked in house.

Portokalopita

The orange cake many guests come back for. 19 reviews mention it, 8 more by its Greek name.

Cyprus coffee and tea

Cyprus coffee, frappé, a large choice of teas, fresh lemonade and fruit juices.

Traditional sweets

Baklava and other homemade sweets that change with the day.

The lane and the plates

Photos from the Google listing of Apomero.

How guests describe a visit

Taken from what guests write in their Google reviews.

Off the busy streets

Apomero means exactly that, guests write: a quiet lane away from the busy streets, with shade and a breeze.

Friendly and quick

Guests describe a smiling team that brings water and cake as soon as you sit down.

For reading and talking

Calm music and small tables, good for a book, a chat or a first date, guests write.

In the old town of Nicosia

Apomero is at Polyviou 24, in a lane of the old town near the Archbishop's Palace. Open from the morning until 23:00.

What guests say

Three of 292 Google reviews, 237 of them with five stars.

“One of my most favourite coffee shops. Wonderful atmosphere. Local vibe. Serving the best portokalopita (orange cake) ever! Large selection of teas, both herbal and non herbal. Clean premises. Friendly staff. A very enjoyable place”

Google review
“I cannot visit Nicosia without stopping at Apomero to ordering as many spinach feta pies and homemade orange cakes possible. The friendly service and the relaxing atmosphere make every visit a pleasure.”

Google review
“I am just in love with the place. Whenever I visit Nicosia, I return. It is exactly what its name says, apomero (=away from the busy streets). Serves coffee, homemade pies and sweets.”
